Human genome sequencing and rapid changes in genome sequencing methods have led to the era of rapidly accumulating genome-sequencing data.
Several types of methods have been developed for representing results of genome sequencing data.
Circular genome visualization tools are critical as they provide rapid interpretation and simple visualization of overall data.
In the last 15 years, circular visualization tools have undergone rapid changes after the development of the circos tool.
Approximately 1-2 circular visualization tools have been published per year since the development of the circos tool.
This study summarizes and revisits all circular genome visualization tools until the third quarter of 2018.
Incidence and mortality of lung cancer have dramatically decreased during the last decades.
Approximately 160,000 deaths per year occurred in the United States due to lung cancer.
Smoking intensity, duration, starting age, as well as environmental cofactors including air pollution, showed strong association with major types of lung cancer.
Lung squamous cell carcinoma is a subtype of non-small cell lung cancer, which represents 25% of the cases.
Exploring the molecular pathogenic mechanisms of lung squamous cell carcinoma plays crucial roles in lung cancer clinical diagnosis and therapy.
Integrative analyses were performed on 299 comparative datasets of RNA-seq and methylation data.
The datasets were collected from 513 lung squamous cell carcinoma cases in The Cancer Genome Atlas.
The data were divided into high and low smoking groups based on smoking intensity (numbers of packs per year).
1002 significantly up-regulated genes and 534 significantly down-regulated genes were identified.
The cellular functions and signaling pathways of these genes were explored using bioconductor packages GOseq and KEGG.
Global methylation status was analyzed and visualized in a circular plot using CIRCOS.
RNA and methylation data were correlatively analyzed, identifying 24 unique genes.
Regional CpG sites' interactive patterns were further investigated using the bioconductor package coMET.
AIRE, PENK, and SLC6A3 were the top 3 genes with significant differences between the high and low smoking groups.
Gene functions of these 24 genes are important in disclosing differences in gene expression caused by different smoking levels.
DNA methylation patterns of these 24 genes are useful in disclosing differences in methylation profiling caused by different smoking levels.
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a common disease of the digestive system with no curative treatments.
Long noncoding RNA tyrosine protein kinase transmembrane receptor 1 antisense RNA 1 (lncRNA ROR1‑AS1) is an lncRNA whose functions have been predicted in human diseases.
The role of lncRNA ROR1‑AS1 in cancer has been probed only in mantle cell lymphoma, not in HCC.
The present study aimed to elucidate the prognostic significance of lncRNA ROR1‑AS1 in HCC.
The Cancer Genome Atlas Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma was used to analyze the expression of ROR1‑AS1 in liver cancer.
χ2 tests were performed to evaluate associations between clinical characteristics and ROR1‑AS1 expression.
The role of ROR1‑AS1 in HCC prognosis was assessed using Kaplan‑Meier curves and proportional hazards model (Cox) analysis.
Gene set enrichment analysis was performed by using a Gene Expression Omnibus dataset.
Multi Experiment Matrix was used to predict genes that may be co‑expressed with ROR1‑AS1.
The Database for Annotation, Visualization and Integrated Discovery and KO‑Based Annotation System were used to analyze the most closely associated cytological behaviors and pathways in HCC.
The genes in the three databases were integrated to screen mRNAs, microRNAs and lncRNAs that had co‑expression relationships with ROR1‑AS1.

Cytoscape, Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes/Proteins and Molecular Evolutionary Genetics Analysis were used to map potential regulatory networks and developmental relationships associated with ROR1‑AS1.
12 genes most closely associated with ROR1‑AS1 were identified, and their relationship was described using a Circos plot.
ROR1‑AS1 was upregulated in HCC, and its expression was related to clinical stage, T stage and N stage.
Kaplan‑Meier curves and Cox analysis indicated that high expression of ROR1‑AS1 was associated with poor prognosis.
ROR1‑AS1 was identified as an independent risk factor for HCC.
Co‑expression data suggested a large regulatory network of 45 genes with indirect associations with ROR1‑AS1.
A small regulatory network of 15 genes with direct or indirect regulatory relationships with ROR1‑AS1 was identified.
A special regulatory network containing 12 genes directly associated with ROR1‑AS1 was identified.
High expression of ROR1‑AS1 suggests poor prognosis in patients with HCC.
Gastric carcinoma (GC) refers to a common digestive system disease that exhibits a very high incidence.
MicroRNA hsa-mir-3923 belongs to a type of miRNA, of which the function has been merely investigated in breast, pancreatic cancers and pre-neoplastic stages of gastric cancer.
The function of hsa-mir-3923 has not been studied or reported in gastric carcinoma.
The relationship between gastric hsa-mir-3923 expression and the clinical features and pathology of GC cases was examined.
This study employed data mining for analyzing gastric carcinoma data in The Cancer Genome Atlas database.
A Chi-squared test was performed for assessing the relations of hsa-mir-3923 expression with clinical and pathology-regulated variables.
The role of hsa-mir-3923 in the prognostic process was assessed using Kaplan-Meier curves, Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis, and proportional hazards model (Cox) study.
Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) was carried out using the Gene Expression Omnibus.
The common miRNA database was compared to predict potential target genes.
Co-expression analysis revealed that a regulatory network probably existed, containing hsa-mir-3923.

Databases for Annotation, Visualization and Integrated Discovery (David) and KO-Based Annotation System (KOBAS) were adopted for analyzing the most tightly associated cytological behavior and pathway in GC.
Cytoscape, R, and STRING were employed for mapping probable regulatory networks displaying relations to hsa-mir-3923.

hsa-mir-3923 displayed up-regulation in gastric carcinoma.
hsa-mir-3923 was associated with vital status, N stage, and histologic grade when expressed.
The predicted results of miRNA target genes suggested a close relationship between 66 genes and hsa-mir-3923 in gastric cancer.

hsa-mir-3923 high-expression reveals poor prognosis of GC patients.
Circos is a highly flexible software package for the circular visualization of complex datasets.
Circos is especially popular in the field of genomic analysis.
Circos enables interactive graphing of analytical data from alternative scientific domains and non-scientific data.
The flexibility of Circos comes with a high degree of complexity.
The complexity of Circos may present an obstacle for researchers not trained in programming or the UNIX command line.
The Galaxy platform provides a user-friendly browser-based graphical interface.
The Galaxy platform incorporates a broad range of 'wrapped' command line tools to facilitate accessibility.
A Galaxy wrapper for Circos has been developed.
The combination of Circos and the Galaxy platform simplifies the specification and configuration of Circos plots for end users.
The combination retains the power to produce publication-quality visualizations of complex multidimensional datasets.
Galactic Circos enables the creation of publication-ready Circos plots using only a web browser via the Galaxy platform.
Users may download the full set of Circos configuration files of their plots for further manual customization.

High throughput next generation sequencing technologies and improved assembly algorithms have resulted in the accumulation of voluminous genomic data in public domains.
The accumulation of genomic data has enabled large scale comparative genome studies, particularly the identification of conserved syntenic blocks among species.
Conserved syntenic blocks facilitate understanding the evolutionary importance of conservation and variation in genomic organization.
Synteny construction and visualization require computational and bioinformatics skills to prepare input files for the synteny analysis pipeline.
Syntenic information in fishes is still in its early stages and is scattered across different research domains.
We present a web-based tool 'Evol2Circos' to provide a user-friendly GUI- and web-based tool for synteny construction and visualization.
Evol2Circos facilitates browsing syntenic information of different fishes using circos, bar, dual, and dot plots.
The information generated from Evol2Circos can be used for further downstream analyses.
Evol2Circos software tool is tested under Ubuntu Linux.
The web-browser, source code, documentation, user manual, example dataset, and scripts for Evol2Circos are available online at: 203.190.147.148/evole2circos/.
Variant allele frequencies (VAF) are an important measure of genetic variation that can be estimated at single-nucleotide variant (SNV) sites.
RNA and DNA VAFs are used as indicators of a wide range of biological traits, including tumor purity and ploidy changes, allele-specific expression, and gene-dosage transcriptional response.
A novel methodology is presented to assess gene and chromosomal allele asymmetries and to aid in identifying genomic alterations in RNA and DNA datasets.
The approach is based on analysis of the VAF distributions in chromosomal segments, which are continuous multi-SNV genomic regions.
In each chromosomal segment, variant probability is estimated as a parameter of a random process that can generate synthetic VAF samples closely resembling the observed data.
Variant probability is a biologically interpretable quantitative descriptor of the VAF distribution in chromosomal segments and is consistent with other approaches.
The proposed methodology is applied to data from 72 samples obtained from patients with breast invasive carcinoma (BRCA) from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA).
DNA and RNA VAF distributions from matched RNA and whole exome sequencing (WES) datasets are compared, showing very similar segmentation and estimated variant probability profiles.
A correlation is found between variant probability and copy number alterations (CNA).
Variant probabilities are used to estimate tumor purity, demonstrating good concordance with other approaches (Pearson's correlation between 0.44 and 0.76).
Variant probabilities can serve as a dependable descriptor of VAF distribution, enabling statistical comparison of matched DNA and RNA datasets.
Variant probabilities provide conceptual and mechanistic insights into relations between the structure of VAF distributions and genetic events.

The methodology is implemented in a Matlab toolbox called GeTallele, which provides functions for analysis, statistical assessment, and visualization of Genome and Transcriptome allele frequency distributions.
GeTallele is available at: https://github.com/SlowinskiPiotr/GeTallele.
Production of biofuels from lignocellulosic crop biomass is an alternative to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
The biofuel production involves collecting biomass, breaking down cell wall components, followed by the conversion of sugars to ethanol.
The lignocellulosic biomass comprises 40-50% cellulose, 20-30% hemicellulose, and 10-25% lignin.
Sorghum is a widely adapted energy crop for biofuel production.
Biomass with low lignin, high cellulose, and high hemicellulose contents are exploited to attain maximum biofuel production efficiency.
Resistance to lodging, pest, disease, and abiotic stresses related to cell wall components is well documented.
Quantitative trait loci were identified to understand the genetic correlation of these traits.
Selection for reduced lignin and increased cellulose content in stover can increase the ethanol yield.
The Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) is a complementary approach to evaluating the marker and phenotype associations among large diversity panels.
Single nucleotide polymorphisms were scanned to identify loci associated with the traits of interest.

In this study, the GWAS was performed on 245 sorghum minicore genotypes to analyze agronomic traits (days to 50% flowering, fresh biomass yield, dry biomass yield) and cell wall components (cellulose, hemicellulose, and lignin).
In-silico validation of the candidate genes was performed using global gene expression data from large-scale RNA sequencing studies in sorghum available in the NCBI GEO database.
The study aims to evaluate native variations in biofuel-related agronomic traits.
The study aims to evaluate native variations in stalk cell wall components.
The study aims to identify significant SNPs or loci related to cell wall components.
An association mapping panel comprising 245 sorghum minicore germplasm accessions was evaluated.
The evaluation was conducted during two post-rainy seasons of 2013 and 2014.
Observations were recorded on the whole plot for days to 50% flowering.
Observations were recorded on the whole plot for fresh biomass yield (tha).
High broad-sense heritability was exhibited for all the traits in individual seasons.
Significant genotype × environment interaction was observed across seasons except for lignin.
Association mapping was performed with a P < 1×10.
This study reports large variability for agronomic and biofuel traits in the sorghum minicore collection with high heritability.
The genetic architecture of cell wall components using the GWAS approach was studied.
Candidate genes for each cell wall component were annotated.
These results give a better understanding of the genetic basis of the sorghum cell wall composition.
The association analysis identified regions of the genome that could be targeted to enhance the quality of biomass and yield.
The identified regions promote breeding efficiency for enhanced biofuel yield.
Gene co-expression network (GCN) mining identifies gene modules with highly correlated expression profiles across samples/conditions.
GCN mining enables researchers to discover latent gene/molecule interactions.
GCN mining helps identify novel gene functions.
GCN mining extracts molecular features from certain disease/condition groups.
GCN mining helps identify disease biomarkers.
There lacks an easy-to-use tool package for users to mine GCN modules that are relatively small in size with tightly connected genes.
GCN modules that are relatively small in size can be convenient for downstream gene set enrichment analysis.
GCN modules may share common members.
To address this need, we developed an online GCN mining tool package: TSUNAMI (Tools SUite for Network Analysis and MIning).
TSUNAMI incorporates the state-of-the-art lmQCM algorithm to mine GCN modules for both public and user-input data.
TSUNAMI supports data types such as microarray, RNA-seq, or any other numerical omics data.
TSUNAMI performs downstream gene set enrichment analysis for the identified modules.
TSUNAMI has a user-friendly interface and provides real-time co-expression network mining through a web server.
TSUNAMI provides direct access and search of NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) databases.
TSUNAMI allows users to input gene expression matrices for GCN module mining.
TSUNAMI offers multiple co-expression analysis tools to choose from.
The co-expression analysis tools in TSUNAMI are highly flexible in regards to parameter selection options.
Identified GCN modules in TSUNAMI are summarized to eigengenes.
Eigengenes are convenient for users to check their correlation with other clinical traits.
TSUNAMI integrates downstream Enrichr enrichment analysis.
TSUNAMI provides links to other gene set enrichment tools.
TSUNAMI enables visualization of gene loci by Circos plot at any step of the process.
The TSUNAMI web service is freely accessible through URL: https://biolearns.medicine.iu.edu/.
The TSUNAMI source code is available at https://github.com/huangzhii/TSUNAMI/.
Clustering is the process of grouping different data objects based on similar properties.
Clustering has applications in various case studies from several fields such as graph theory, image analysis, pattern recognition, and statistics.
There are numerous algorithms and tools able to generate clustering results.
Different algorithms or parameterizations may produce quite dissimilar cluster sets.
The user is often forced to manually filter and compare clustering results to decide which generate the ideal clusters.
This study presents VICTOR, the first fully interactive and dependency-free visual analytics web application for comparing clustering results.
VICTOR allows the visual comparison of the results of various clustering algorithms.
VICTOR can handle multiple cluster set results simultaneously and compare them using ten different metrics.
Clustering results can be filtered and compared using data tables, interactive heatmaps, bar plots, correlation networks, sankey plots, and circos plots.
VICTOR's functionality is demonstrated using three examples.
In the first example, five different network clustering algorithms are compared on a Yeast protein-protein interaction dataset.
In the second example, four different parameters of the MCL clustering algorithm are tested on the same dataset.
In the third example, four different meta-analyses with hierarchically clustered differentially expressed genes involved in myocardial infarction are compared.
VICTOR is available at http://victor.pavlopouloslab.info or http://bib.fleming.gr:3838/VICTOR.
Type B adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are iatrogenic immune-mediated syndromes with mechanistic etiologies that remain incompletely understood.

Some of the most severe ADRs, including delayed drug hypersensitivity reactions, are T-cell mediated, restricted by specific human leukocyte antigen risk alleles and sometimes by public or oligoclonal T-cell receptors (TCRs).
T-cell receptors (TCRs) are central to the immunopathogenesis of tissue-damaging responses in severe ADRs.
The specific cellular signatures of effector, regulatory, and accessory immune populations that mediate disease, define reaction phenotype, and determine severity have not been defined.

Recent development of single-cell platforms bringing together advances in genomics and immunology provides tools to simultaneously examine the full transcriptome, TCRs, and surface protein markers of highly heterogeneous immune cell populations at the site of the pathological response at a single-cell level.

The requirement for advanced bioinformatics expertise and computational hardware and software has often limited the ability of investigators with the understanding of diseases and biological models to exploit these new approaches.
We describe the features and use of a state-of-the-art, fully integrated application for analysis and visualization of multiomic single-cell data called Visual Genomics Analysis Studio (VGAS).
VGAS is a unique user-friendly, Windows-based graphical user interface specifically designed to enable investigators to interrogate their own data.
VGAS includes tools for sequence alignment and identification of associations with host or organism genetic polymorphisms.

VGAS enables analysis of single-cell TCR-RNA-Cellular Indexing of Transcriptomes and Epitopes by Sequencing (CITE-seq), allowing holistic cellular characterization by unbiased transcriptome and select surface proteome.

VGAS does not require user-directed coding or access to high-performance computers, instead incorporating performance-optimized hidden code to provide application-based fast and intuitive tools for data analyses and production of high-resolution publication-ready graphics on standard specification laptops.
VGAS allows analyses of comprehensive single-cell TCR sequencing (scTCR-seq) data, detailing functional pairings of α-β heterodimer TCRs.
VGAS provides one-click histograms to display entropy and gene rearrangements.
VGAS generates Circos and Sankey plots to visualize clonality and dominance.

For unbiased single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analyses, VGAS enables users to extract cell transcriptome signatures according to global structure via principal component analysis, t-distributed stochastic neighborhood embedding, or uniform manifold approximation and projection plots.
VGAS allows overlay of scTCR-seq data to identify and select immunodominant TCR-expressing populations.
VGAS integrates sequence-based detection of surface protein markers using oligo-labeled antibodies (CITE-seq) to provide comparative understanding of surface protein expression.
VGAS enables differential gene or protein analyses visualized using volcano plot or heatmap functions.

VGAS allows comparison of data to reference cell atlases or suitable controls to reveal discrete disease-specific subsets, from epithelial to tissue-resident memory T-cells, and activation status, from senescence through exhaustion.
VGAS enables visualization of more finite transcript expression using violin and box plots.
Guided tutorial videos are available for VGAS, as are regular application updates based on the latest advances in bioinformatics and user feedback.
The dramatic development of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technologies has spurred research interest in decoding cell-cell communication.
Several in-silico methods have been developed to study cell-cell communication.
Most existing methods lack the ability to predict communication pathways connecting the insides and outsides of cells.
CellCall is a toolkit developed to infer inter- and intracellular communication pathways by integrating paired ligand-receptor and transcription factor (TF) activity.
CellCall uses an embedded pathway activity analysis method to identify significantly activated pathways involved in intercellular crosstalk between certain cell types.
CellCall offers a rich suite of visualization options, including Circos plot, Sankey plot, bubble plot, and ridge plot, to present analysis results.

Case studies on scRNA-seq datasets of human testicular cells and the tumor immune microenvironment demonstrated the reliable and unique functionality of CellCall in intercellular communication analysis and internal TF activity exploration.
The functionality of CellCall in intercellular communication analysis and internal TF activity exploration was further validated experimentally.
Comparative analysis of CellCall and other tools indicated that CellCall was more accurate and offered more functions.
CellCall provides a sophisticated and practical tool for deciphering intercellular communication and related internal regulatory signals based on scRNA-seq data.
CellCall is freely available at https://github.com/ShellyCoder/cellcall.
Whole genome and exome sequencing (WGS/WES) are the most popular next-generation sequencing (NGS) methodologies.
WGS/WES are often used to detect rare and common genetic variants of clinical significance.
Automated sequence data processing, management, and visualization should be an indispensable component of modern WGS and WES data analysis.
Automated sequence data processing is essential for sequence assembly, variant detection (SNPs, SVs), imputation, and resolution of haplotypes.
A newly developed findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable (FAIR) bioinformatics-genomics pipeline, Java-based Whole Genome/Exome Sequence Data Processing Pipeline (JWES), is presented.
JWES is designed for efficient variant discovery, interpretation, and big data modeling and visualization.
JWES is a cross-platform, user-friendly, product line application with three modules: (a) data processing, (b) storage, and (c) visualization.
The data processing module performs tasks for variant calling.
The data storage module efficiently manages high-volume gene-variant data.
The data visualization module supports variant data interpretation with Circos graphs.
The performance of JWES was tested and validated in-house with different experiments using Microsoft Windows, macOS Big Sur, and UNIX operating systems.
JWES is an open-source and freely available pipeline.
JWES allows scientists to take full advantage of all available computing resources without requiring much computer science knowledge.
JWES has been successfully applied for processing, management, and gene-variant discovery, annotation, prediction, and genotyping of WGS and WES data.
JWES has been used to analyze variable complex disorders.
The performance of JWES is reported with reproducible case studies using open access and in-house generated, high-quality datasets.
Large-scale phosphoproteome profiling using mass spectrometry (MS) provides functional insight that is crucial for disease biology and drug discovery.
Extracting biological understanding from phosphoproteomic data is an arduous task requiring multiple analysis platforms that are not adapted for automated high-dimensional data analysis.
An integrated pipeline is introduced to combine several R packages for extracting high-level biological understanding from large-scale phosphoproteomic data.
The pipeline enables seamless integration with existing databases and knowledge resources.

In a single run, PhosPiR provides data clean-up, fast data overview, multiple statistical testing, differential expression analysis, phosphosite annotation and translation across species, multilevel enrichment analyses, proteome-wide kinase activity and substrate mapping, and network hub analysis.
Data output includes graphical formats such as heatmap, box-plots, volcano-plots, and circos-plots.
This resource is designed to assist proteome-wide data mining of pathophysiological mechanisms without a need for programming knowledge.
Multidimensional integrative data analysis of digital phenotyping is crucial for elucidating the pathologies of multifactorial and heterogeneous diseases, such as dry eye (DE).
This crowdsourced cross-sectional study explored a novel smartphone-based digital phenotyping strategy to stratify and visualize the heterogeneous DE symptoms into distinct subgroups.
Multidimensional integrative data were collected from 3,593 participants between November 2016 and September 2019.
Dimension reduction via Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection stratified the collected data into seven clusters of symptomatic DE.
Symptom profiles and risk factors in each cluster were identified by hierarchical heatmaps and multivariate logistic regressions.
Stratified DE subgroups were visualized by chord diagrams, co-occurrence networks, and Circos plot analyses to improve interpretability.
Maximum blink interval was reduced in clusters 1, 2, and 5 compared to non-symptomatic DE.
Clusters 1 and 5 had severe DE symptoms.
A data-driven multidimensional analysis with digital phenotyping may establish predictive, preventive, personalized, and participatory medicine.
Mental health problems will seriously damage social harmony and family happiness.
This paper proposes a study on mental health intelligence assessment based on multisource information fusion.
The multisource information fusion visualization based on the Circos diagram is designed and realized.
The parallel coordinate visualization is established.
The MDS algorithm is used to project multidimensional survey objects into low-dimensional visualization space.
The actual UPI and SCL-90 questionnaire data for 278 students of a certain major at a university provided by the cooperative unit are used.
The results show that the mental health problems of student A are serious, and the symptoms of depression and schizophrenia are prominent.
It is necessary to seek psychological experts for corresponding treatment for student A in time.
Student B's mental health problems are also serious, and the user judges that student B still needs further diagnosis and treatment.
The correlation analysis results of multisource information fusion are roughly the same as the actual situation, which is convincing.
The multisource mental health information fusion of college students has a certain correlation and complementarity.
Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) involved in diquat (DQ) poisoning were identified via bioinformatics analysis.
Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) involved in paraquat (PQ) poisoning were identified via bioinformatics analysis.
Signaling pathways involved in diquat (DQ) poisoning were identified via bioinformatics analysis.
Signaling pathways involved in paraquat (PQ) poisoning were identified via bioinformatics analysis.
The study aims to inform the development of novel clinical treatments for diquat (DQ) and paraquat (PQ) poisoning.
Raw data from GSE153959 were downloaded from the Gene Expression Omnibus database.
DEGs of the DQ vs. control (CON) and PQ vs. CON comparison groups were identified using R.
DEGs shared by the two groups were identified using TBtools.
The shared DEGs were searched in the Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) databases.
The Database for Annotation, Visualization, and Integrated Discovery was used for the search.
A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed.
Hub genes were identified using the cytoHubba plug-in in Cytoscape software.
Circos and contrast plots showing the DEGs shared between mouse and human chromosomes were constructed using TBtools.
Thirty-one DEGs shared by the DQ and PQ groups were identified.
Enriched biological process terms included positive regulation of cell proliferation and translation.
Enriched cellular component terms included extracellular region, intracellular membrane-bounded organelle, and mitochondrion.
Enriched molecular function terms included transcription factor activity and sequence-specific double-stranded DNA binding.
Enriched KEGG pathways included the interleukin-17 signaling pathway, tumor necrosis factor signaling pathway, and human T-cell leukemia virus 1 infection.
These pathways may serve as targets for gene therapy.
These DEGs may serve as targets for gene therapy.
Multi-CSAR is a web server that can efficiently and more accurately order and orient the contigs in the assembly of a target genome into larger scaffolds based on multiple reference genomes.
Multi-CSAR identifies sequence markers shared between the target genome and each reference genome.
Multi-CSAR computes a scaffold for the target genome based on each single reference genome.
Multi-CSAR combines all the single reference-derived scaffolds into a multiple reference-derived scaffold.
To run Multi-CSAR, users need to upload a target genome to be scaffolded and one or more reference genomes in multi-FASTA format.
Users can choose to use the 'weighting scheme of reference genomes' for Multi-CSAR to automatically calculate different weights for the reference genomes.
Users can choose either 'NUCmer on nucleotides' or 'PROmer on translated amino acids' for Multi-CSAR to identify sequence markers.

In the output page, Multi-CSAR displays its multiple reference-derived scaffold in two graphical representations (i.e. Circos plot and dotplot) for users to visually validate the correctness of scaffolded contigs.
Multi-CSAR displays its multiple reference-derived scaffold in a tabular representation to further validate the scaffold in detail.
Multi-CSAR is available online at http://genome.cs.nthu.edu.tw/Multi-CSAR/.
Wet-aged tuna is a high-value processed aquatic product that has become a popular food.
The lipidomics characteristics of wet-aged tuna during the aging process have not been investigated.
Lipidomics phenotypic data of tuna at different wet-aging stages were acquired using iKnife rapid evaporative ionization mass spectrometry.
Dominant lipid components, including fatty acid (FA), phosphatidylcholine (PC), phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), and phosphatidylinositol (PI), were structurally identified.
Principal component analysis, permutation test, heatmap, and circos plot analysis were performed to characterize lipids in wet-aged tuna.
Big data and data analysis methods and models are important tools in food security studies.
Big data and data analysis methods are used for gap analysis in food security studies.
Big data and data analysis models are used for preparation of appropriate analytical frameworks in food security studies.
These innovations necessitate the development of novel methods for collecting data.
These innovations necessitate the development of novel methods for storing data.
These innovations necessitate the development of novel methods for processing data.
These innovations necessitate the development of novel methods for extracting data.
The primary goal of this study was to conduct a critical review of agricultural big data and methods and models used for FS studies published in peer-reviewed journals since 2010.
Approximately 130 articles were selected for full content review after the pre-screening process.

There are different sources of data collection, including online databases, the internet, omics, Internet of Things, social media, survey rounds, remote sensing, and the Food and Agriculture Organization Corporate Statistical Database.
The collected data require analysis.
There are certain FS gaps both worldwide and in the United Arab Emirates that need to be addressed by scientists and policymakers.
The identification of the drivers, policies, and indicators is necessary.
The findings of this review could be used to develop an appropriate analytical framework for FS and nutrition.
Extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) of chromosomal origin is found in many eukaryotic species and cell types, including cancer.
EccDNAs with oncogenes drive tumorigenesis.
Most studies of eccDNA employ short-read sequencing for their identification.
Short-read sequencing cannot resolve the complexity of genomic repeats, which can lead to missing eccDNA products.
Long-read sequencing technologies provide an alternative to constructing complete eccDNA maps.
We present a software suite, Construction-based Rolling-circle-amplification for eccDNA Sequence Identification and Location (CReSIL), to identify and characterize eccDNA from long-read sequences.
CReSIL's performance in identifying eccDNA, with a minimum F1 score of 0.98, is superior to the other bioinformatic tools based on simulated data.
CReSIL provides many useful features for genomic annotation, which can be used to infer eccDNA function.
CReSIL provides Circos visualization for eccDNA architecture investigation.
We demonstrated CReSIL's capability in several long-read sequencing datasets, including datasets enriched for eccDNA and whole genome datasets from cells containing large eccDNA products.
The CReSIL suite software is a versatile tool for investigating complex and simple eccDNA in eukaryotic cells.
T cell immune dysfunction is a prominent characteristic of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL).
T cell immune dysfunction is the main cause of failure for immunotherapy and multi-drug resistance in CLL.
There remains a lack of specific biomarkers for evaluating T cell immune status with outcome for CLL patients.
T cell factor 1 (TCF1) is encoded by the genome.
PlasMapper 3.0 is a web server that allows users to generate, edit, annotate and interactively visualize publication quality plasmid maps.
Plasmid maps are used to plan, design, share and publish critical information about gene cloning experiments.
PlasMapper 3.0 is the successor to PlasMapper 2.0 and offers many features found only in commercial plasmid mapping/editing packages.
PlasMapper 3.0 allows users to paste or upload plasmid sequences as input.
PlasMapper 3.0 allows users to upload existing plasmid maps from its large database of >2000 pre-annotated plasmids (PlasMapDB).
The PlasMapDB database can be searched by plasmid names, sequence features, restriction sites, preferred host organisms, and sequence length.
PlasMapper 3.0 supports the annotation of new or never-before-seen plasmids using its own feature database.
The feature database contains common promoters, terminators, regulatory sequences, replication origins, selectable markers and other features found in most cloning plasmids.
PlasMapper 3.0 has several interactive sequence editors/viewers that allow users to select and view plasmid regions, insert genes, modify restriction sites or perform codon optimization.
The graphics for PlasMapper 3.0 have been substantially upgraded.

PlasMapper 3.0 now offers an interactive, full-color plasmid viewer/editor that allows users to zoom, rotate, re-color, linearize, circularize, edit annotated features and modify plasmid images or labels.
PlasMapper 3.0 enables users to improve the esthetic qualities of their plasmid map and textual displays.
All the plasmid images and textual displays are downloadable in multiple formats.
PlasMapper 3.0 is available online at https://plasmapper.ca.
Cell-to-cell communication (CCC) plays important roles in multicellular organisms.

The identification of communication between cancer cells themselves and between cancer cells and normal cells in the tumor microenvironment helps understand cancer genesis, development, and metastasis.
CCC is usually mediated by Ligand-Receptor Interactions (LRIs).
We developed a Boosting-based LRI identification model (CellEnBoost) for CCC inference.

Potential LRIs are predicted by data collection, feature extraction, dimensional reduction, and classification based on an ensemble of Light gradient boosting machine and AdaBoost combining convolutional neural network.
The predicted LRIs and known LRIs are filtered.
The filtered LRIs are applied to CCC elucidation by combining CCC strength measurement and single-cell RNA sequencing data.
CCC inference results are visualized using heatmap view, Circos plot view, and network view.
The experimental results show that CellEnBoost obtained the best AUCs and AUPRs on the collected four LRI datasets.
A case study in human head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) tissues demonstrates that fibroblasts were more likely to communicate with HNSCC cells.
This finding is in accord with the results from iTALK.
We anticipate that this work can contribute to the diagnosis and treatment of cancers.
Much of the human genetics variant repertoire is composed of single nucleotide variants (SNV) and small insertion/deletions (indel).
Structural variants (SV) remain a major part of our modified DNA.
SV detection has often been a complex question to answer because of the necessity to use different technologies to detect each category of SV.
Technologies for SV detection include array CGH, SNP array, Karyotype, and Optical Genome Mapping.
Whole Genome Sequencing is required to achieve appropriate resolution for SV detection.
Human geneticists are accumulating SV data thanks to the deluge of pangenomic analysis.
The interpretation of structural variants remains time consuming and challenging.
The AnnotSV webserver aims to annotate and interpret SV potential pathogenicity in the context of human diseases.
The AnnotSV webserver aims to recognize potential false positive variants from all the SV identified.
The AnnotSV webserver aims to visualize the patient variants repertoire.
The most recent developments in the AnnotSV webserver include updated annotation sources and ranking.
The most recent developments in the AnnotSV webserver include three novel output formats to allow diverse utilization such as analysis and pipelines.
The most recent developments in the AnnotSV webserver include two novel user interfaces, including an interactive circos view.
Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) using oligonucleotide-based probes is an innovative modification of classic FISH techniques.
FISH using oligonucleotide-based probes enables karyotypic identifications.
The design and in silico visualization of oligonucleotide-based probes derived from the Cucumis sativus genome are described.
The probes are plotted comparatively to the closely related Cucumis melo genome.
The visualization process is realized in R using various libraries for linear or circular plots including RIdeogram, KaryoploteR, and Circlize.
CCPlotR is an R package that generates visualizations of cell-cell interactions.
CCPlotR is designed to work with the output of tools that predict cell-cell interactions from single-cell gene expression data.
CCPlotR requires only a table of predicted interactions as input.
The package can generate a comprehensive set of publication-ready figures such as heatmaps, dotplots, circos plots, and network diagrams.
CCPlotR provides a useful resource for researchers working on cell-cell interactions.
CCPlotR is available to download and install from GitHub.
CCPlotR comes with a toy dataset to demonstrate the different functions.
Support for users will be provided via the GitHub issues tracker.
River and reservoir bacterial communities are the most basic part of river biomes and ecosystem structure, and play an important role in river biological processes.
It remains unclear how highly regulated dam reservoirs affect both soil and sediment bacterial communities.
A temporal distribution pattern of bacterial communities was investigated using Illumina MiSeq sequencing in a transition section of the Three Gorges Reservoir (TGR).
In total, 106,682 features belong to the bacteria kingdom, encompassing 95 phyla, 228 classes, 514 orders, 871 families, 1959 genera, and 3,053 species.
With water level regulation, Shannon diversity index and observed species differed significantly, with no significant difference in Simpson evenness.
Both in the high water level period (October) and the low water level period (June), Proteobacteria, Acidobacteri, and Chloroflexi were the most abundant phyla.
Based on PCA plots and Circos plot, the microbial community structure has changed significantly.
LEfSe method was used to identify the classified bacterial taxa with significant abundance differences between the low water level and high water level periods.
KOs (KEGG Orthology) pathway enrichment analysis was conducted to investigate functional and related metabolic pathways in groups.
It can be inferred that water level regulation affects community growth by affecting the metabolism of the microbial community.

Late-maturity alpha-amylase (LMA) is a wheat genetic defect causing the synthesis of high isoelectric point alpha-amylase following a temperature shock during mid-grain development or prolonged cold throughout grain development, both leading to starch degradation.
The physiology of LMA is well understood.
The biochemical mechanisms involved in grain LMA response remain unclear.
High-throughput proteomics was applied to 4,061 wheat flours displaying a range of LMA activities.
An array of statistical analyses was used to select LMA-responsive biomarkers.
The selected biomarkers were mined using a suite of tools applicable to wheat proteins.
LMA-affected grains activated their primary metabolisms such as glycolysis and gluconeogenesis.
LMA-affected grains activated the TCA cycle.
LMA-affected grains activated DNA- and RNA-binding mechanisms.
LMA-affected grains activated protein translation.
Protein folding activities were driven by chaperones and protein disulfide isomerase.
Protein assembly occurred via dimerisation and complexing.
The secondary metabolism was mobilized with the upregulation of phytohormones.
The secondary metabolism was mobilized with the upregulation of chemical and defence responses.
LMA invoked cellular structures, including ribosomes, microtubules, and chromatin.
LMA expression greatly impacted grain storage proteins, as well as starch and other carbohydrates.
LMA upregulated alpha-gliadins and starch metabolism.
LMA downregulated LMW glutenin, stachyose, sucrose, UDP-galactose, and UDP-glucose.
This is the first proteomics study tackling the wheat LMA issue.
This is the largest plant-based proteomics study published to date.
Logistics, technicalities, requirements, and bottlenecks of a large-scale high-throughput proteomics experiment are discussed.
Challenges associated with big data analyses are discussed.
Since the approval of the first chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T product in 2017, the number of new CAR-T clinical trials worldwide exceeds 100 per year.
1649 clinical studies have been conducted to explore possible future clinical applications of targets or target pairs through different biotechnologies.
In this study, we aim to take a data-driven analytical approach to explore potential dual-target pairs based on clinical trial information.
We screened 1283 non-withdrawal interventional CAR-T clinical trials spanning 96 different targets and 74 target pairs from clinicaltrials.gov.
Through the Circos plot and temporal network plots, the information between targets and indications was visualized.
Based on the assumption that two targets of a target pair must target the same indication, five new target pairs were inferred, including CD19/CD7, CD19/CD5, CD19/CD37, and CD19/BAFFR.
The inferred target pairs were validated by expression pattern, literature, and patent information.
This study provides novel support for target profiling of CAR-T from the perspective of clinical trials.
This study provides a reference for researchers and developers to select new targets or target pairs of CAR-T cell therapy.
Byu d Mar 25 (BM25) has been verified to have neuroprotective effects in Alzheimer's disease (AD) mice.
The molecular mechanism of BM25's neuroprotective effects remains unclear.
The study aimed to investigate the expression profiling of lncRNAs and circRNAs by microarray analysis.
Six hippocampus samples from LPS-mediated AD mice model treated with normal saline (NS) (n=3) and AD mice model treated with BM25 (n=3) were selected.
Microarray analysis was performed to detect the expression profiles of lncRNAs and circRNAs in hippocampus.
Differentially expressed (DE) lncRNAs, mRNAs, and circRNAs were identified through scatter plot and volcano plot filtering with a threshold of fold-change ≥2 and P ≤ 0.05.
Co-expression network analysis was performed using Circos software.
Cis- and Trans-regulation were analyzed using RIsearch-2.0 and FEELNC softwares.
LncRNA-transcription factors (TFs) and LncRNA-Target-TFs network were analyzed by Clusterprofiler software.
The prediction of miRNAs binding to circRNAs was performed with miRNAbase.
A total of 113 DElncRNAs, 117 DEmRNAs, and 4 DEcircRNAs were detected.
The pathway analysis showed the mRNAs correlated with lncRNAs were involved in apoptosis, inflammatory mediator regulation of TRP channels, NF-kappa B, and PI3K-Akt signaling pathway.
The lncRNA-TFs network analysis suggested the lncRNAs were mostly regulated by Ncoa1, Phf5a, Klf6, Lmx1b, and Pax3.
The lncRNA-target-TFs network analysis indicated that GATA6, Junb, Smad1, Twist1, and Mafb mostly regulate the same lncRNAs: XR_001783430.1 and NR_051982.1.
480 miRNAs were predicted to bind to 4 identified circRNAs.
BM25 may affect Alzheimer's disease by regulating the expression of lncRNAs and circRNAs, which could regulate the expressions of mRNAs or miRNAs through the LncRNA-Target-TFs network.
As different taxa evolve, gene order often changes slowly enough that chromosomal 'blocks' with conserved gene orders (synteny) are discernible.

The MCScanX toolkit was published in 2012 as freely available software for the detection of 'colinear blocks' and subsequent synteny and evolutionary analyses based on genome-wide gene location and protein sequence information.
MCScanX provides a powerful tool for conducting diverse synteny and evolutionary analyses due to its simplicity and high efficiency for colinear block detection.
The detection of colinear blocks has been embraced as an integral step for pangenome graph construction.
New application trends of MCScanX are explored to better connect this tool to other tools and accelerate insight generation from exponentially growing sequence data.

A detailed protocol is provided covering how to install MCScanX on diverse platforms, tune parameters, prepare input files from data from the National Center for Biotechnology Information, run MCScanX and its visualization and evolutionary analysis tools, and connect MCScanX with external tools, including MCScanX-transposed, Circos, and SynVisio.
This protocol is easily implemented by users with minimal computational background and is adaptable to new data of interest to them.
The data and utility programs for this protocol can be obtained from http://bdx-consulting.com/mcscanx-protocol.
Tools for visualizing genomes are essential for investigating genomic features and their interactions.
Tools originally designed for animal mitogenomes and plant plastomes are used to visualize the mitogens of plants.
Existing tools cannot accurately display features specific to plant mitogenomes, such as nonlinear exon arrangement for genes.
Plant mitogenomes have features like the prevalence of functional noncoding features and complex chromosomal architecture.
A software package, plant mitochondrial genome map (PMGmap), was developed using the Python programming language to address these problems.
PMGmap can draw genes at exon levels.
PMGmap can draw cis- and trans-splicing gene maps, noncoding features, and repetitive sequences.
PMGmap can scale genic regions by using the scaling of the genic regions on the mitogenome (SAGM) algorithm.
PMGmap can draw multiple chromosomes simultaneously.
Compared with other state-of-the-art tools, PMGmap showed better performance in visualizing 405 plant mitogenomes.
PMGmap shows potential as an invaluable tool for plant mitogenome research.
The web and container versions and the source code of PMGmap can be accessed through the following link: http://www.1kmpg.cn/pmgmap.
Recent studies have demonstrated a role for Ten-Eleven Translocation-2 (TET2), an epigenetic modulator, in regulating germinal center formation and plasma cell differentiation in B-2 cells.

A tandem repeat is a sequence of nucleotides that appear as multiple contiguous, near-identical copies arranged consecutively.

The study deepened the understanding of gene regulation by noncoding RNAs in the TGF-β2-induced fibrogenic changes in HTM cells.
The study deepened the understanding of the anti-fibrotic activity of silibinin in HTM cells.

The Gram-stain-negative bacterium Paracoccus spp., from the class Alphaproteobacteria and family Rhodobacteraceae, exhibits exceptional metabolic flexibility, diverse substrate utilization, and tolerance to abiotic stressors.
Comprehensive sequencing, phylogenetic, and physiological characterization were performed between two strains of the genus, Paracoccus pantotrophus DSM 11073 and Paracoccus sp. AS002.
Illumina sequencing yielded a total genome size of 4.2 Mbp for P. pantotrophus DSM 11073.
Illumina sequencing yielded a total genome size of 4.8 Mbp for Paracoccus sp. AS002.
Through phylogenetic analysis using the EDGAR software, Paracoccus sp. AS002 shared with Paracoccus versutus DSM 582 the same clade in the phylogenetic tree.
Paracoccus sp. AS002 had an ANI score of 98.9 %, indicating that it could be reclassified as P. versutus AS002.
The study compared various attributes of the sequenced genomes and highlighted the metabolic versatility of the genus Paracoccus.

The use of a wide substrate panel demonstrated the metabolic versatility of the strains, including the PET monomer ethylene glycol, the C1 carbon source formic acid, and renewable carbon sources such as ethanol.
The ability of the strains to produce bioplastic was assessed.
P. pantotrophus DSM 11073 produced 36 % polyhydroxybutyrate (% cell dry weight) on glucose and 40 % on 60 mM ethylene glycol.
P. versutus AS002 produced 28 % polyhydroxybutyrate (% cell dry weight) on glucose and 16 % on 60 mM ethylene glycol.
This study demonstrates the value of sequencing bacterial strains for biotechnological applications.
The study highlights EDGAR's effectiveness in phylogenetic analysis.
The findings pave the way for using Paracoccus as a microbial chassis in sustainable biotechnological processes supporting the circular bioeconomy.
Plasmids are a common tool in biotechnology to deliver recombinant DNA into microbial cells for the production of enzymes, pharmaceutical proteins, chemicals, or metabolites.
A stable plasmid system that provides reliable gene expression over generations is essential for the successful utilization of single-cell organisms in research and production applications.
Most Komagataella phaffii expression clones are generated by the integration of linear plasmids into the genome.
Circular episomal plasmids are not stable under non-selective conditions in Komagataella phaffii.

The low rate of homology-directed specific integration and the large variation among transformants of random integration limit the application of Komagataella phaffii in enzyme engineering approaches or comparative studies.
High transformation rates and uniform expression levels are desired for enzyme engineering approaches or comparative studies.

In the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae, the problem of circular plasmid stability and partition to daughter cells during mitosis has been solved by combining centromeric sequences or elements of the 2-micron plasmid with an autonomously replicating sequence (ARS) that serves as an origin of replication.
Similar attempts to solve the problem of circular plasmid stability have not yet been successful or widely adapted in Komagataella phaffii.
Permanent selection pressure is required to maintain episomal plasmids in Komagataella phaffii.
There are no reports so far about functional 2-micron plasmids for Pichia pastoris.
CEN/ARS plasmids for Pichia pastoris are usually rather large and do not provide the high transformation rates as known for episomal plasmids of Saccharomyces cerevisiae expression systems.
The availability of a broad set of resistance, auxotrophic, and carbon source utilization markers facilitates reliable plasmid selection in small-scale screening applications.
The availability of a broad set of resistance, auxotrophic, and carbon source utilization markers has recently proved to be successful for bioreactor-scale expression.
The combined advantages of high transformation rates and low clonal variability of ARS plasmids can be exploited.
This article describes the successful utilization of ARS1-containing plasmids in Komagataella phaffii.
The ARS1-containing plasmids include antibiotic-free selection, complementation of knockout strains, and application of CRISPR/Cas by transient gRNA and CAS9 gene expression in Komagataella phaffii.

CIRI3 is a tool for circRNA detection and quantification in terabyte-scale RNA-sequencing datasets.
CIRI3 uses dynamic multithreaded task partitioning for processing.
CIRI3 employs a blocking search strategy for junction reads.
CIRI3 is an order of magnitude faster than existing tools.
CIRI3 provides increased accuracy compared to existing tools.
Differentially spliced circRNAs were identified across 2,535 cancer-related samples.
A pretraining model and a biomarker network were constructed.

Thrombosis and hemorrhage are common complications in maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients, potentially attributed to platelet dysfunction.
This study aimed to investigate platelet autophagy in MHD patients through whole transcriptome sequencing of platelets.
A total of 24 MHD patients and 24 healthy individuals (normal controls) were enrolled.
RNA sequencing was performed on platelets, and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using the DESeq2 package.

Functional enrichment analyses, including gene ontology, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes, and gene set enrichment analysis, were conducted to explore the biological functions and signaling pathways of DEGs.
Protein-protein interaction analysis, hub gene identification, and machine learning algorithms were applied to predict key autophagy-related genes (ATGs).

Competing endogenous RNA networks (circular RNA [circRNA]-microRNA-messenger RNA [mRNA]) and circRNA-mRNA co-expression networks were constructed to reveal regulatory mechanisms of autophagy in platelets.
A total of 8798 mRNAs were identified as differentially expressed.
Gene set enrichment analysis revealed that these DEGs were significantly enriched in pathways such as focal adhesion and platelet activation, with positive enrichment scores.
Protein-protein interaction and hub gene analysis identified Beclin 1, Sequestosome 1, ATG16L1, ATG12, and ATG7 as central ATGs with high interaction degrees.

Machine learning approaches, including least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression, support vector machine, and random forest, further identified Caspase 8, C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 4, vascular endothelial growth factor A, and forkhead box O3 as key autophagy-associated genes in MHD patients.
A total of 8842 circRNAs were identified as differentially expressed, and 2739 target mRNAs were predicted from these differentially expressed circRNAs.
Among them, 168 circRNAs were associated with ATGs.
In the circRNA-mRNA co-expression network, 42 circRNAs and 22 mRNAs were implicated in autophagy regulation.
In the competing endogenous RNA network, 17 circRNAs, 40 microRNAs, and 20 mRNAs were identified as potential components involved in platelet autophagy regulation.
Key ATGs and regulatory networks were identified in MHD platelets, revealing potential mechanisms of dysfunction.
These findings offer insights into thrombosis and bleeding risks and may aid in developing targeted therapies.
Genomic loci and genome-independent DNA exhibit heterogeneous dynamics related to physiological function.
Live-cell imaging of non-repetitive sequences is essential for studying genomic dynamics.
Live-cell imaging of non-repetitive sequences is limited by low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
Low SNR restricts accurate identification and dynamic tracking of non-repetitive sequences.
The development of a BRIGHT system for non-repetitive sequence live imaging is reported.
BRIGHT stands for bivalent near-infrared nanobody-mediated cascade illumination of genomic loci for high-SNR tracking.
BRIGHT employs dCas9-n×ALFA to target genomic loci.
BRIGHT realizes high SNR by triggering cascade-dependent illumination.
BRIGHT uses bivalent binding and antigen-dependent illumination of a bivalent near-infrared fluorescent nanobody targeting ALFA tags (Bi-NIR-Fb).
The mitochondrial genome (mitogenome) has recently emerged as an essential tool for investigating evolutionary relationships of organisms.

The complete mitogenome of a Collembola species, Troglopedetes meridionalis Jantarit, Surakhamhaeng & Deharveng, 2020 (Entomobryidae, Paronellinae), was sequenced using low-coverage whole-genome sequencing techniques.
The circular mitogenome is 14,785 bp and contains 37 genes, including 22 transfer RNAs (tRNAs), 13 protein coding sequences (CDS), and two ribosomal RNA (rRNAs).
The nucleotide composition analysis revealed that the stop codon of all protein-coding genes, except COX2, is TAA.
Phylogenetic analysis, incorporating representative other species of Entomobryidae, indicates that the subfamily Paronellinae is monophyletic.
Phylogenetic analysis shows that T. meridionalis and T. dispersus Deharveng & Gers, 1993 are closely related.
This phylogenetic framework offers a valuable reference for future research on the evolutionary relationships within Paronellinae and the broader Entomobryidae family.
In Thailand, the distribution of Troglopedetes Joseph, 1872 is largely restricted to areas north of the Isthmus of Kra.
The closely related genus Cyphoderopsis Carpenter, 1917 is confined to the southern region of Thailand.
A distribution map illustrating the geographic ranges of both genera within Thailand is also provided.

Shotgun metagenomic data analysis for investigating biogeochemical cycles in the environment remains challenging due to the steep learning curve, intensive time investment, and high computational demands.
These challenges pose significant barriers for many researchers.
We present a new R package called 'CNPS.cycle,' designed to streamline the interpretation of shotgun metagenomic data related to biogeochemical processes.
The CNPS.cycle package provides visually informative outputs.
The package comprises four distinct analysis modules focused on carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur cycling.

Users can utilize the package by uploading annotation result files derived from shotgun metagenomic data based on the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes and the NCBI non-redundant protein sequence database.
The package automates essential steps, including data preprocessing, curation, and differential analysis of biogeochemical cycle-related genes.
The package also automates the analysis of microorganisms possessing biogeochemical cycle-related genes at the contig level.
The package includes β-diversity analysis and data visualization.
The outcome is a comprehensive analysis revealing differentially abundant genes and functionally significant microbial entities associated with the carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur cycles.
The results are presented in the form of tables and high-quality images.
This tool provides profound insights into the relationship between soil microorganisms and elemental chemical cycles.
The tool advances our comprehension of soil ecosystems.
The CNPS.cycle package is available on GitHub (https://github.com/yuezhengfu/CNPS.cycle).
Detailed instructions on the usage of the package can be found on the project's GitHub page (https://github.com/yuezhengfu/CNPS.cycle/wiki).
The 'CNPS.cycle' R package simplifies the analysis of shotgun metagenomic data related to biogeochemical cycles.
The 'CNPS.cycle' R package has significant environmental implications.
The automated workflow of 'CNPS.cycle' identifies key genes and microbes involved in carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, and sulfur cycling.
The tool enhances understanding of microbial contributions to ecosystem functions.
The 'CNPS.cycle' tool enables researchers to explore microbial-mediated nutrient cycling more efficiently.
The tool supports informed decisions in environmental management and climate change mitigation.
By providing accessible, high-quality outputs, 'CNPS.cycle' facilitates data-driven insights into the interplay between microbes and global biogeochemical processes.
Plant research faces persistent challenges in integrating heterogeneous data and ensuring compatibility across diverse analytical pipelines.
The limited automation of existing tools often results in fragmented workflows, reducing analytical efficiency and reproducibility.
SPDEv3.0 was developed as a fully integrated bioinformatics platform with a graphical user interface.
SPDEv3.0 consolidates more than 130 functions across seven logically connected modules.
SPDEv3.0 streamlines key tasks such as gene family identification, primer design, and genome feature extraction through high-level automation.
SPDEv3.0 enables users to perform complex bioinformatic workflows with minimal manual intervention.
Collinearity analysis between Arabidopsis thaliana and A. halleri can be completed in under 2 min using only genome and annotation files, with all intermediate steps executed automatically.
SPDEv3.0 offers over 30 customizable visualization functions, including genomic feature mapping, domain structure illustration, heatmaps, Circos plots, and statistical charting.
The visualization functions in SPDEv3.0 are designed to help users generate publication-ready figures without coding.
A total of 40 classical breeding methods have been implemented in SPDEv3.0.
All 40 classical breeding methods in SPDEv3.0 support automated computation following user data input.
Benchmarking across a range of plant genomes, including those exceeding 14 Gb, demonstrates SPDEv3.0's robust performance, scalability, and practical utility.
SPDEv3.0 integrates high automation, module interoperability, and extensive visualization capacity.
SPDEv3.0 provides a powerful and accessible solution for modern plant genomics and breeding research.
Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are increasingly recognized as important regulators of splicing, transcription, and gene expression.
Circular RNAs (circRNAs) may contribute to drug resistance.
The purpose of this study was to investigate the potential roles of circRNAs in the development of albendazole (ABZ) resistance in Haemonchus contortus (H. contortus).
The study analyzed the numbers, species, structural characteristics, and functions of circRNAs.
Regulatory networks were constructed to provide insight into circRNA-mediated mechanisms associated with ABZ resistance.
ABZ-sensitive (ABZ-S) strains of H. contortus were subjected to high-throughput sequencing.
ABZ-resistant (ABZ-RA) strains of H. contortus were subjected to high-throughput sequencing.
ABZ-resistant treatment (ABZ-RB) strains of H. contortus were subjected to high-throughput sequencing.
cDNA library construction was performed for ABZ-S, ABZ-RA, and ABZ-RB strains of H. contortus.
Illumina HiSeq was used for high-throughput sequencing and cDNA library construction.
A total of 5695 circRNAs were identified across the three strain comparisons, with lengths ranging from 126 to 95,630 nt.
364 unique DEcircRNAs were identified in ABZ-S.
252 unique DEcircRNAs were identified in ABZ-RA.
311 unique DEcircRNAs were identified in ABZ-RB.
These DEcircRNAs were associated with 1369 parental genes involved in 974 GO terms and 326 KEGG pathways, including 86 metabolic pathways.
Complex competitive endogenous RNA (ceRNA) regulatory networks were constructed among DEcircRNAs, differentially expressed microRNAs (DEmiRNAs), and differentially expressed messenger RNAs (DEmRNAs).
The ceRNA network comprised 110 DEcircRNAs, 41 DEmiRNAs and 10 DEmRNAs.
35 components of the ceRNA network were related to metabolism.
37 components of the ceRNA network were related to organismal systems.
Validation experiments confirmed expression differences for nine DEcircRNAs.
The high-throughput identification of DEcircRNAs in drug-resistant strains suggests that some circRNAs may participate in the development of ABZ resistance.
Some circRNAs may regulate source genes and function as ceRNAs in the development of ABZ resistance.
These regulatory processes may involve pathways such as ABC transporters.
These regulatory processes may involve pathways such as drug metabolism-cytochrome P450.

Shotgun metagenomic sequencing is used to uncover genes encoding novel biocatalysts from complex environments.
A new FAD-dependent D-lactate dehydrogenase (PdG-D-LDH) was discovered and characterized.
The new FAD-dependent D-lactate dehydrogenase (PdG-D-LDH) was identified from the gut microbiome of the isopod.
This study illustrates how metagenomics, structural biology, and computational tools can jointly drive the discovery of new enzymes with valuable biotechnological applications.
The study aligns with circular economic principles.

Novel plasma assays enabled accurate blood-based biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases with minimally invasive options for clinical use.
Large-scale studies encompassing multiple neurodegenerative diseases using novel multiplex platforms are essential to uncover disease-specific biomarkers and pathways.

We generated and analyzed plasma biomarker data using the NULISAseq™ CNS Panel from 3,232 participants with Alzheimer disease (AD), Dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), Frontotemporal dementia (FTD), Parkinson disease (PD) and cognitively unimpaired individuals, from the Charles F. and Joanne Knight Alzheimer Disease Research Center.
We identified proteins associated with disease status and AD-related phenotypes (Clinical Dementia Rating®, CSF Aβ42/Aβ40, Amyloid-PET, and Tau-PET).
These proteins were used to identify disease-specific biomarkers and perform pathway analyses.
We identified 81 proteins associated with AD, 21 with DLB, four with FTD, and 52 with PD after multiple test correction.
Disease comparison showed that PD and DLB had the highest similarity, followed by AD and DLB.
Each disease also presented disease-specific signatures.
Some AD-specific proteins included p-tau217; MSLN and SAA1 were specific to DLB, and FLT1 and PARK7 to PD.
We identified eight proteins associated with Amyloid-PET, eight with Tau-PET, 14 with CSF Aβ42/40 ratio, and 72 with CDR, some of which were specific to each phenotype.
We used a data-driven approach to identify the p-tau217 cut-off for biomarker positivity.
Plasma p-tau217 achieved an AUC of 0.81 (95% CI: 0.79-0.83) for AD diagnosis and 0.96 (95% CI: 0.94-0.98) for Amyloid positivity.
P-tau217 had 93.77% agreement with Amyloid-PET status.
Proteins associated with AD were enriched in protein-lipid complex binding pathway, whereas PD associated proteins were enriched in laminin-related pathways.
FTD associated proteins were enriched in cytoskeleton proteins.
This is the largest plasma NULISA CNS study performed till date and covers the four major neurodegenerative diseases: AD, PD, DLB and FTD.
We validated the high classification accuracy of the NULISA plasma p-tau217 and its strong correlation with Amyloid-PET status.
We identified disease-specific proteins that could enhance differential diagnosis.
These findings highlight the potential of the NULISA platform as a reliable quantitative tool for research and clinical applications in neurodegenerative diseases.
The innate immune response is started immediately following brain ischemia, resulting in adaptive immunity.
Experimental evidence indicates that the immune response caused by cerebral ischemia plays a crucial role during initial brain damage and subsequent brain injury recovery.
Molsidomine, a nitric oxide donor, has been found to reduce schizophrenia-like behavioral abnormalities in rats due to glutamate hypofunction.
The current study sought to explore the efficacy of molsidomine versus conventional drugs in cerebral ischemia.
This study scavenges literature to retrieve various genes like PI3K, MMP9, COX2, LOX, TLR4, AKT1, mTOR, NLRP3, STAT3, IL1β, NFκB, TNF, IL6, and TP53 involved in cerebral ischemia.
A two-step molecular docking revealed significant gene-drug complexes followed by a protein-protein interaction (PPI).
Oncoprint analysis, protein-protein interaction, and functional and pathway enrichment associated with these genes are incorporated in this study.
A circos plot depicting the mutational profile of the genes is incorporated in this study.
This comprehensive in-silico approach reveals the efficacy of the potency of the candidate drug, molsidomine in treating cerebral ischemia.
Plasmids are extrachromosomal mobile genetic elements that often carry genes responsible for antimicrobial resistance.
Plasmid epidemiology aims to track the evolution and spread of plasmids.
The field of plasmid epidemiology currently faces significant barriers that make practical implementation using whole genome sequence data difficult.
Hybrid-assembled genomes remain the most reliable way to identify and track complete plasmids.
Most genomic surveillance data exists in the form of short-read sequencing, which lacks the resolution required to accurately resolve plasmids.
Despite recent advances, long-read-only assemblies have not yet reached the consistency seen in hybrid assemblies.

The ideal approach to plasmid epidemiology using whole genome sequence data would consider the limitations of sequencing technologies and the constraints of existing genomic surveillance infrastructure, in addition to the unique evolutionary biology of plasmids.

ACCIO (Assembly-based Circular Contig Identification for Outbreaks) is a tool which creates a reference plasmid database and uses it to infer which plasmids, and genetically related plasmid groupings, are present in an input assembly (Illumina, Nanopore, or hybrid assembly).
ACCIO was validated using an internal dataset of 303 plasmid-harboring bacterial clinical and surveillance isolates collected from a single acute tertiary care center.
When highly related database plasmids were grouped together, ACCIO achieved 100% sensitivity and 92.1% positive predictive value (PPV) for detection of plasmid groups using hybrid assemblies.
ACCIO demonstrated comparably strong performance for Illumina assemblies with 93.0% sensitivity and 86.6% PPV.
ACCIO demonstrated comparably strong performance for Nanopore assemblies with 79.3% sensitivity and 91.4% PPV.
Evaluation of ACCIO on three external datasets yielded consistently high performance.
When benchmarked against MOB-suite, a tool for reconstruction and typing of plasmids, ACCIO demonstrated superior performance across nearly all assembly types and plasmid grouping levels.
ACCIO integrates database construction, clustering, and plasmid calling into a single workflow compatible with all major sequencing platforms.
ACCIO is intended to help advance plasmid epidemiology beyond its current technological and infrastructural barriers.
The study investigates the associations of systolic blood pressure (SBP) with retinal arterial structure assessed by OCT.
The study investigates the associations of arterial stiffness, measured via the cardio-ankle vascular index (CAVI), with retinal arterial structure assessed by OCT.
The study examines age-related differences in these associations.
A cross-sectional analysis was conducted.
The analysis focused on a community-based Japanese cohort.
A total of 6969 adults underwent OCT imaging between 2012 and 2016.
The mean age of participants was 57.6 years.
69.6% of participants were women.
Peripapillary circular OCT B-scans were used to assess the 4 largest retinal arteries.
OCT-derived parameters included outer diameter (OD), inner diameter (ID), wall thickness, and wall reflectivity.
Multivariable linear regression adjusted for demographic, ocular, and systemic covariates.
Interaction analyses evaluated age modification.
Analyses were stratified by age (<65 vs. ≥65 years).
OCT-based measurements of outer diameter (OD).
OCT-based measurements of inner diameter (ID).
OCT-based measurements of wall thickness.
OCT-based measurements of wall reflectivity.
Higher SBP was associated with smaller OD (β = -0.136, 95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.151 to -0.120).
Higher SBP was associated with smaller ID (β = -0.136, 95% CI: -0.150 to -0.121).
The CAVI was positively associated with wall reflectivity (β = 0.371, 95% CI: -0.081 to 0.822).
Interaction analyses indicated age-related modification (SBP × age for OD: β = 0.005; ID: β = 0.005; CAVI × age for wall reflectivity: β = 0.030).
In participants aged <65 years, the inverse associations of SBP with OD were stronger (β = -0.186) than in those aged ≥65 years (β = -0.076).

For CAVI, no clear association with wall reflectivity was found in participants aged <65 years (β = -0.165).
For CAVI, a positive association with wall reflectivity was observed in participants aged ≥65 years (β = 0.725).
OCT-based retinal arterial measurements revealed age-dependent associations with systemic vascular factors.
In younger adults, elevated SBP was linked to narrower arterial diameters, reflecting functional vasoconstriction.
In older adults, greater wall reflectivity was associated with arterial stiffness, suggesting structural remodeling.
These findings support OCT as a noninvasive tool for assessing different stages of microvascular aging.
Confirmation in longitudinal studies is warranted.

A case-control study was performed to investigate the association between polymorphisms in the circSirt1 flanking introns and susceptibility to myocardial infarction (MI).
This study included 541 coronary artery disease (CAD) cases and 278 controls.
Four SNPs, including rs33957861, rs2273773, rs145758730, and rs34416841 in the circSirt1 gene, were genotyped.
Genotyping was conducted utilizing the polymerase chain reaction-ligation detection reaction (PCR-LDR) technique.
The associations of these SNPs with susceptibility were analyzed using multivariate logistic regression.
Haplotype analysis was performed using SHEsis software.
The C allele of rs34416841 was significantly associated with an increased risk of MI (adjusted OR = 1.65, 95% CI = 1.07–2.56, P = 0.024).
Consistent trends were observed in co-dominant models (OR = 1.70, 95% CI = 1.04–2.77, P = 0.034).
Consistent trends were observed in dominant models (OR = 1.73, 95% CI = 1.07–2.79, P = 0.025).
The C allele of rs34416841 specifically increased progression risk from stable CAD to MI (OR = 1.62, 95% CI = 1.09–2.42, P = 0.018).
Stratified analyses demonstrated stronger associations among younger individuals (≤ 60 years), males, smokers, non-drinkers, and hypertension subjects.
The C-T-C-G haplotype containing the rs34416841C allele was associated with increased MI risk (OR = 1.43, 95% CI = 1.03-2.00, P = 0.035).
No statistically significant association was observed between the rs34416841 polymorphism and CAD risk across all tested genetic models.
The rs34416841 polymorphism is located within an Alu element in the flanking intron of circSirt1.
The rs34416841 polymorphism demonstrates significant associations with MI susceptibility in the Han Chinese population.
The rs34416841 polymorphism demonstrates significant associations with CAD progression in the Han Chinese population.
Anhedonia is a core symptom of major depressive disorder (MDD).
The study aimed to validate the Dimensional Anhedonia Rating Scale (DARS).
The study aimed to explore data-driven subgroups of anhedonia among individuals with depression.
The study aimed to determine associations of anhedonia with anxiety, suicidal ideation, neuroticism, and childhood trauma.

DARS food and drinks score was associated with early-life physical abuse and anxiety.
