DNA plasmids are widely used for delivering proteins and RNA in genome editing.
Bacterial components in DNA plasmids can lead to inactivation, cell toxicity, and reduced efficiency compared to minicircle DNA (mcDNA).
Minicircle DNA (mcDNA) lacks bacterial sequences.
Existing commercial kits recombine plasmids into mcDNA within proprietary bacterial strains.
Commercial kits are labor-intensive, yield inconsistent results, and often produce endotoxin-contaminated low-quality mcDNA.
Plasmid2MC is a novel cell-free method developed to address the challenges of existing mcDNA preparation methods.
Plasmid2MC utilizes ΦC31 integrase-mediated recombination to efficiently excise the bacterial backbone from conventionally prepared plasmids.
Plasmid2MC includes digestion of the bacterial backbone and all other DNA contaminants.
Plasmid2MC results in highly pure and virtually endotoxin-free mcDNA.
We demonstrated the application of mcDNA to express CRISPR-dCas9 for base editing in HEK293T cells and mouse embryonic stem cells.
We demonstrated the application of mcDNA for homology-independent targeted insertion (HITI) genome editing.
The method's ease of preparation, high efficiency, and the high purity of the resulting mcDNA make Plasmid2MC a valuable tool for applications requiring bacterial backbone-free circular DNA.
Assessing the accuracy of long-read assemblies from complex environmental metagenomes is challenging.
Environmental metagenomes include underrepresented organisms.
Four state-of-the-art long-read assembly software programs were benchmarked: HiCanu, hifiasm-meta, metaFlye, and metaMDBG.
The benchmarking was conducted on 21 PacBio HiFi metagenomes spanning mock communities, gut microbiomes, and ocean samples.
Read clipping events were quantified to identify where assemblies diverge from their source reads.
Read clipping events occur when long reads are systematically split during mapping to maximize agreement with assembled contigs.
Long-read metagenome assemblies can include more than 40 errors per 100 million base pairs of assembled contigs.
Errors in long-read metagenome assemblies include multi-domain chimeras, prematurely circularized sequences, haplotyping errors, excessive repeats, and phantom sequences.
An open-source tool and a reproducible workflow are provided for rigorous evaluation of assembly errors.
The workflow charts a path toward more reliable genome recovery from long-read metagenomes.
Hepatitis B and C viruses (HBV and HCV) remain among the leading causes of liver disease worldwide.
Current antiviral drugs, such as nucleotide analogues (NAs), can reduce the replication of new HBV and HCV infections but cannot completely eliminate chronic infections.
A stable form of viral DNA, known as covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA), persists in liver cells and continues to sustain the infection.
The CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing system has emerged as a powerful tool for precisely cutting and inactivating specific DNA sequences.
Researchers have applied CRISPR/Cas9 in numerous studies to directly target and disrupt the HBV genome, demonstrating promising antiviral effects in both cell cultures and animal models.
Targeting multiple sites within the HBV genome has been shown to further enhance its effectiveness.
This approach paves the way for potential combination therapies aimed at disabling both cccDNA and HBV and HCV DNA integrated into the host genome.

CRISPR/Cas9 still faces significant challenges before clinical application, most notably the risk of off-target effects and the difficulty of delivering the system efficiently into liver cells in vivo.
Future progress will depend on improving the tool's precision, efficiency, flexibility, and delivery methods.
Recent advances in designing guide RNAs (gRNAs) for targeting HBV and HCV have been explored.
Delivery systems used to transport CRISPR/Cas9 into cells have been studied.
Remaining challenges and potential strategies for advancing CRISPR/Cas9 from the laboratory toward a viable clinical cure for HBV and HCV are discussed.
Circular RNA (circRNA) represents a critical class of regulatory RNAs with distinctive structural and functional features.
The functions of circRNAs are modulated by various RNA modifications.
CircRM is a nanopore direct RNA sequencing-based computational method for profiling RNA modifications in circRNAs at single-base and single-molecule resolution.
CircRM integrates circRNA detection, read-level modification detection, and quantitative assessment of methylation rates.
CircRM identified 427 high-confidence circRNAs.
CircRM enables systematic characterization of three major modifications: m5C (AUC = 0.855), m6A (AUC = 0.817), and m1A (AUC = 0.769).
CircRM revealed distinct modification patterns compared with linear RNAs, highlighting RNA-type-specific regulations.
Key features of circRNA-specific modifications, such as the enrichment near the back-splice junctions, were identified.
Cross-cell line analyses demonstrated conserved and cell-type-specific modification patterns.
These findings reveal a unique epitranscriptomic landscape associated with circRNAs at the computational level.
CircRM establishes itself as a powerful tool for advancing the study of RNA modifications in circular RNA biology.
CircRM is freely accessible at: https://github.com/jiayiAnnie17/CircRM.
Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a cardiovascular condition.
AAA is characterized by the abnormal dilation of the abdominal aorta.
A circular RNA (circRNA) microarray was utilized.
The microarray identified differentially expressed circRNAs.
The study focused on angiotensin II (Ang II)-stimulated AAA mice.
Male apolipoprotein E-deficient (apoE-/-) mice were randomly assigned to 2 groups and subjected to 28 days of infusion with either Ang II or saline.
At the end of the experiment, the mice were euthanized via exsanguination under anesthesia.
The periadventitial tissues were carefully removed from the aortic wall to measure the maximal external diameter of the suprarenal aorta.
The periadventitial tissues were then stored for further analysis.

Circular nucleic acids such as extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) and circular RNA (circRNA) are increasingly recognized for their biological relevance.

The detection of circular nucleic acids remains challenging due to tool-specific biases.
The detection of circular nucleic acids is hindered by limited validation frameworks.
The detection of circular nucleic acids is affected by high variability in performance across datasets.
We benchmarked 10 circle detection tools across diverse conditions.
The benchmarking used both simulated and biological datasets.
Our evaluation included classical performance metrics.
Our evaluation included a novel internal measure of read distribution symmetry ($\Delta$CJ) to assess circle prediction confidence.
We explored the impact of sequencing protocols on circle detection.
We explored the impact of filtering strategies on circle detection.
We explored the impact of combined tool consensus on circle detection.
Detection accuracy was highly influenced by sequencing depth.
Detection accuracy was highly influenced by alignment algorithm.
Detection accuracy was highly influenced by experimental enrichment protocols.

Electroactive microorganisms (EAMs) can be incorporated into active soil management as a strategy for regenerative agriculture.

EAMs also produce bioelectricity through extracellular electron transfer.

Soil microbial fuel cells serve as platforms for bioremediation.

This review positions EAMs as a tool in soil management for shaping climate-smart, regenerative agroecosystems that sustain productivity and ecological balance.
Recent advances in biomanufacturing have stimulated the exploration of microbial platforms for pigment production, offering alternatives to plant-derived and synthetic colorants.
Microbial carotenoids are a group of naturally occurring pigments with vibrant red, orange, and yellow coloration and demonstrated antioxidant capacity and health-promoting benefits.
Sporobolomyces pararoseus is one of the most well-studied oleaginous red yeasts.

This review summarizes current knowledge on Sporobolomyces pararoseus as a promising microbial cell factory for carotenoid production.
The review emphasizes the distinctive biological characteristics and environmental adaptability of Sporobolomyces pararoseus.
The review highlights enzymatic pathways governing carotenoid synthesis in Sporobolomyces pararoseus.
The review discusses state-of-the-art biotechnological interventions to enhance productivity and recovery efficiency of carotenoids in Sporobolomyces pararoseus.
The review explores potential commercial applications of Sporobolomyces pararoseus across diverse biotechnology sectors.

Integrated solutions employing CRISPR-based genome editing techniques, multi-omics profiling approaches, circular bioeconomy strategies, and comprehensive safety evaluation procedures are proposed.
The review synthesizes contemporary scientific understanding with innovative bioprocessing techniques.
The review connects fundamental insights into Sporobolomyces pararoseus biology with actionable methodologies for commercial-scale implementation.
Sporobolomyces pararoseus could serve as a microbial platform for sustainable production of β-carotene, torulene, and torularhodin to meet global market demands.
The natural occurrence of 2,6-diaminopurine (Z) as a substitute for adenine (A) in certain bacteriophage genomes has profound evolutionary implications and promising biotechnological potential.
Progress in this field has been stymied by the absence of reliable methods to detect dZ-DNA, particularly in mixed samples, and to distinguish A from Z at the single-nucleotide level.
Z-Calling is a machine learning-based tool designed to identify dZ-DNA and discriminate A/Z bases directly from PacBio Circular Consensus Sequencing (CCS) reads without additional processing.
Z-Calling analyzes sequence context-dependent kinetic signal changes induced by Z/A substitution.
Z-Calling achieves exceptional sensitivity, reliably detecting dZ-DNA even in samples with as little as ~1% dZ-DNA content.
The A/Z base-calling module of Z-Calling demonstrates robust performance, with AUC scores of 0.942-0.952 across diverse DNA sequence contexts.
Z-Calling represents a significant advancement in accessible and accurate dZ-DNA sequencing, paving the way for its broader application in biotechnology.
Z-Calling is freely available at https://github.com/xiaochuanle/Z-Calling.

We aimed to identify prognostic biomarkers specific to HBV-HCC patients.

Hub genes were identified using Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes (STRING) Cytohubba protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis.
Survival analysis of hub genes was plotted.

circADGRL2 showed the highest upregulation (~25-fold).

The target mRNAs of miRNAs were predicted to be associated with several cancer pathways, such as MAPK and RAS.

The lack of immuno-competent animal models of hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection has been an obstacle to vaccine development and research on immune responses.
Hepacivirus ratti (Norway rat hepacivirus-1: NRHV1) is a virus closely related to HCV that specifically infects the liver and induces hepatocellular carcinoma in rats.

NRHV1 expressing a reporter gene serves as a powerful tool for analyzing the in vivo dynamics and pathogenicity mechanisms of NRHV1.
In this study, we developed a reporter NRHV1 capable of infection and replication in both immunodeficient mice and cultured cells.
We established a platform for generating diverse reporter viruses.
A reporter virus containing the HiBiT gene in the coding region of NS5A domain III was constructed using circular polymerase extension reaction (CPER).
Infection with this reporter virus led to HiBiT activity in infected cells.
The HiBiT activity was correlated with the amount of intracellular viral RNA.
This reporter virus established persistent infection in NOD-SCID mice and led to the generation of HiBiT activity in the livers of infected mice.
Loss of the HiBiT gene was observed in some mice.
Reporter virus recovered from infected mice could infect and generate HiBiT activity in cultured cells.

This platform provides a versatile tool for in vitro quantitative antiviral screening and for exploring viral infection dynamics in vivo.
Further studies will be required to improve the long-term stability of the HiBiT reporter.

Extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) has transitioned from genomic curiosity to a pivotal regulator at the intersection of genomics and immunology.
This review synthesizes recent advances in eccDNA biology, elucidating its integral roles in both innate and adaptive immunity and its pathogenic contributions to autoimmune diseases.
eccDNA arises from diverse genomic events, including DNA damage repair, replication stress, and chromothripsis.

In innate immunity, eccDNA functions as a potent damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP), activating cytosolic sensors like cGAS-STING and AIM2 to drive type I interferon and pro-inflammatory cytokine responses.

In the adaptive immune system, eccDNA is not merely a byproduct of processes such as V(D)J recombination (e.g., TRECs, KRECs); it also acts as an active modulator regulating immune gene expression via enhancer-like activity, influencing antigen presentation, and shaping T and B cell development.
Aberrant eccDNA accumulation is implicated in the pathogenesis of autoimmune disorders such as systemic lupus erythematosus and rheumatoid arthritis.
Plasma eccDNA levels not only correlate with clinical disease activity indices but also track with therapeutic response, positioning eccDNA as a powerful non-invasive biomarker.
Targeting eccDNA biogenesis or its sensing pathways represents a promising therapeutic frontier for restoring immune homeostasis.
Future research integrating single-cell omics and longitudinal profiling is poised to dissect cell-specific functions and unlock the full clinical potential of eccDNA.

Collectively, these findings establish eccDNA as both a functional regulator and a diagnostic tool, offering novel insights into the fundamental interplay between genomic integrity and immune function.
Phylogenetic trees are central to biology.
Most published phylogenetic trees are available only as visual diagrams and not in the machine-readable Newick format.
Thousands of published phylogenetic trees in the scientific literature are unavailable for follow-up analyses, comparisons, and supertree construction.
Experts can easily read phylogenetic tree diagrams.
The manual construction of a Newick string from a diagram is laborious, error-prone, and time-consuming.
Previous attempts to semi-automate the reading of tree images relied on image processing techniques.

Image processing techniques often encounter difficulties with typical published tree diagrams containing various graphical elements and annotations that overlap the branches, such as error bars on internal nodes.
Treemble is a user-friendly desktop application for generating Newick strings from tree images.
The user of Treemble simply clicks to mark node locations, assisted by a deep learning-based node detection tool.
Treemble algorithmically assembles the tree from the node coordinates alone.
Treemble facilitates the automatic reading of tip name labels.
Treemble can be used for both rectangular and circular trees.
Treemble is a native desktop application for macOS and Windows.
Treemble is freely available with documentation at treemble.org.
The source code for Treemble is available at github.com/John-Allard/Treemble.
The trained node detection model is available at huggingface.co/John-Allard/treemble-1.

The symbiotic bacterium Xenorhabdus magdalenensis has a complex life cycle that alternates between a mutualistic relationship with the native entomopathogenic nematode Steinernema australe and a pathogenic stage with the insect host.
Several nematode-bacteria relationships are well studied, but the S. australe-X. magdalenensis complex, originally isolated from southern Chile, remains poorly understood.
This study provides the first complete circular 4.086 Mb genome of the Xenorhabdus magdalenensis IMI397775 strain.
The study genomically and chemically describes the bacteria at their ecological stages: in the IJs' receptacle as symbionts and in the insect's hemolymph as pathogens.
A genomic analysis of X. magdalenensis IMI397775 was conducted using genmarks and Prokka for functional annotation.
Comparative tools were used to assess the evolutionary history of the most related Xenorhabdus spp.
Genomic data were integrated with biochemical metabolic profiling using the API 50 CG test to validate the genotype-phenotype relationship.
The architecture of the IMI397775 strain is characterized by 20 rearrangements relative to X. doucetiae, its closest relative, suggesting a rapid evolutionary diversification.
The identification of 25 BCGs with low similarity to known databases, over 60% of which may encode novel molecule positions, makes this strain an important reservoir for natural product discovery.
In vivo evaluation of cell-free supernatant confirms that the genomic potential of this strain may be a potent biological tool with high efficacy.
The strain is a potential candidate for the development of new-generation biopesticides.

Neuroimmune signaling across the peripheral-vascular-glial axis is increasingly recognized as a driver of both age-related brain vulnerability and the earliest stages of neurodegenerative disease, including Alzheimer disease.
Evaluating the peripheral-vascular-glial axis in vivo remains challenging due to limited neuroinflammatory imaging biomarkers.

We utilized [11C]CS1P1 positron emission tomography (PET) to quantify sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 (S1PR1) availability alongside plasma proteomics in 42 cognitively normal individuals (age 21-82).
Differential abundance analysis and structural equation modeling (SEM) were used to identify a multi-compartment neuroimmune cascade.
The neuroimmune cascade links peripheral T-cell activation (CD40LG), vascular endothelial disruption (ICAM1/TEK), central S1PR1 upregulation, and reactive astrogliosis (GFAP).
Mediation analysis estimated that the S1PR1 axis accounts for 25.5% of the total effect of CD40LG on GFAP.
This neuroimmune cascade appears coupled to the astrocytic immune response and is exacerbated by underlying amyloid-beta pathology.
These findings suggest [11C]CS1P1 may serve as an in vivo tool for evaluating peripheral-to-central immune crosstalk.
Synthetic genomics is advancing from microbial toward multicellular organisms.
Current manual methods for DNA and genome assembly remain inadequate for the efficient, large-scale production of long DNA constructs.
We present Programmed DNA Assembly via Cas9 and Conjugative Transfer (PACT).
PACT integrates a linear vector system, bacterial conjugation, and programmable Cas9-mediated cleavage to achieve highly efficient, iterative assembly of large DNA fragments.
PACT enhances assembly efficiency by ~30-fold compared to conventional circular vector strategies.
PACT enables one-step assembly of DNA up to 80 kb.
We engineered four single guide-RNA-Marker donor cassettes to support iterative assembly workflows.
PACT can utilize low-recombination Escherichia coli strains as hosts to efficiently assemble Arabidopsis thaliana mitochondrial genome with high repeat units.
Integrated with an automated robotic platform, we developed an unattended, high-throughput pipeline (aPACT) toward large-scale parallel DNA assembly.
Using aPACT, we successfully assembled three large DNA constructs: a 210 kb digital DNA, the designed chloroplast (120 kb) and mitochondrial (350 kb) genome of A. thaliana.
This automated system offers a powerful tool for scalable assembly of large DNA molecules.
This system accelerates synthetic genomics research toward complex multicellular organisms.

Mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy plays a crucial role in mitochondrial function, aging, and a wide range of human diseases.
Recent advances in high-throughput sequencing have enabled large-scale detection of heteroplasmic variants.
Effective cohort-level integration, comparison, and visualization of Mutant Allele Frequency (MAF) values remain challenging.
Existing tools often focus on single-sample visualization or require substantial manual preprocessing, limiting their scalability and usability for large cohorts.
We developed Mito_Plot, an open-source computational pipeline designed for standardized quantification of Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) heteroplasmy across multiple samples.
Mito_Plot provides intuitive visualization of Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) heteroplasmy across multiple samples.
Mito_Plot accepts standard mitochondrial VCF files.
Mito_Plot automatically calculates MAF based on allelic depth information.
MAF data from multiple samples are aggregated into a unified matrix aligned by genomic position.
The unified matrix enables direct cross-sample comparison.
The pipeline provides interactive two-dimensional circular plots that map MAF onto the mitochondrial genome with gene-level annotations.
The circular plots facilitate rapid identification of mutation hotspots and sample-specific patterns.
Mito_Plot offers optional three-dimensional visualizations.
The three-dimensional visualizations enhance exploration of large cohorts by separating variant distributions across samples and genomic regions.
Application of Mito_Plot to multi-sample mitochondrial sequencing datasets demonstrated robust handling of both variants with low and high MAF values.
Mito_Plot demonstrated efficient processing of large cohorts.
Mito_Plot demonstrated improved interpretability compared with static or single-sample visualizations.
Mito_Plot is a scalable, user-friendly software pipeline for cohort-scale quantification and visualization of mtDNA MAF.
Mito_Plot integrates standardized MAF calculation with interactive 2D and 3D visualizations.
Mito_Plot facilitates comprehensive exploration of mitochondrial variant landscapes across large datasets.

Resistance genes are critical for plant defence against biotic stresses.

207,353 SSR markers and 141,582 miRNAs associated with resistance genes were detected.

The global prevalence of metabolic diseases (MetDs) continues to rise and is associated with an increased cancer risk.
Genome-wide association studies have identified numerous single nucleotide variants (SNVs) linked to MetDs.
Some single nucleotide variants linked to MetDs are within genes also implicated in tumorigenesis.
G-quadruplexes (G4s) are non-canonical DNA secondary structures that regulate gene expression in diverse and context-dependent ways.
Variants affecting G4 structure may alter transcriptional efficiency.
Disease-associated variants are frequently located within or near regulatory elements.
Disease-associated variants may overlap with cancer-associated alternative promoters.
We systematically assess the overlap between MetD-associated SNVs and G4 motifs.
We evaluate the effects of MetD-associated SNVs on G4 stability, topology, and their potential to modulate the regulatory activity of G4s in alternative promoters.
Approximately 0.9% to 1.6% of MetD-associated SNVs are located within G4 motifs (G4-SNVs), depending on the prediction tool.
Effect alleles, those associated with risk or protection against MetDs, generally reduce G4 stability, regardless of their direction of association.
Several G4-SNVs are mapped to cancer-associated alternative promoters.
The destabilizing MICB rs2855804 C/T variant is mapped to a cancer-associated alternative promoter.
The stabilizing PLA2G6 rs2277844 G/A variant is mapped to a cancer-associated alternative promoter.
In vivo G4 formation is confirmed by permanganate/S1 nuclease footprinting coupled with sequencing.
Circular dichroism spectroscopy reveals allele-specific changes in G4 topology and stability.
Integration of Hi-C data, histone modifications, transcription factor binding, and luciferase reporter assays further support the regulatory impact of G4-SNVs.
G4-SNVs are unlikely to be the sole disease drivers.
G4-SNVs significantly influence transcriptional regulation.
G4-SNVs potentially contribute to allele-specific gene expression in MetD patients.
G4-SNVs are linked to increased cancer risk in MetD patients.
The prevalence of Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is increasing at an alarming rate globally.
There is a need for a digital tool that enables continuous and real-time data collection.
A digital tool can help overcome stigma and improve mental health awareness.
We describe mHealth, an open-source, scalable mobile health application.
The mHealth application is compatible with iPhone operating systems (iOS) and Android.

The mHealth application was built using Xamarin, an open-source framework.

Cell and gene therapy (CGT) manufacturing has outpaced traditional chemistry, manufacturing, and controls frameworks, leaving a 'black box' in vector quality control (QC).

Legacy assays such as Sanger and short-read next-generation sequencing often fail to resolve complex structures including adeno-associated virus (AAV) inverted terminal repeats, lentiviral recombination, and mRNA poly(A) tails.
Oxford Nanopore Technologies enables long-read, native single-molecule sequencing to access these attributes directly.
This review summarizes nanopore sequencing across the CGT lifecycle.
For plasmid DNA, nanopore sequencing confirms full-length circular identity and reveals structural heterogeneity missed by restriction mapping.

For viral vectors (AAV and lentivirus), nanopore sequencing functions as an integrity assay to distinguish full genomes from truncations and to detect sequence-resolved impurities, including reverse-packaged plasmid backbones.
For mRNA therapeutics, direct RNA sequencing profiles poly(A) tail length distributions and base modifications.
Rhodotorula toruloides is an emerging oleaginous yeast with strong potential as a microbial cell factory for the production of acetyl-CoA-derived bioproducts.
Engineering of R. toruloides has been limited by the absence of a functional episomal plasmid system.
A functional episomal plasmid system is a foundational genetic tool for rapid gene expression, pathway testing, and CRISPR-based genome engineering.
We report the first episomal plasmid system for R. toruloides.
Through systematic screening of candidate autonomously replicating sequences (ARSs) from diverse sources, we identified multiple functional ARS elements.
We selected C63F4, a fragment derived from Contig 63 of R. toruloides CBS14, because of its stable performance.
The resulting pC63F4 plasmid was maintained episomally, supported GFP reporter expression, exhibited a copy number of 2.39 ± 0.13, and showed good stability during long term cultivation.
To overcome poor transformation efficiency, we developed a Cre-loxP-mediated in vivo re-circularization strategy that enabled reliable delivery of the episomal plasmid.

Using this improved system, we demonstrated functional episomal expression of metabolic engineering genes and multi-gene pathways for the production of triacetic acid lactone, fatty alcohols, and limonene.
We leveraged this platform to establish a redesigned CRISPR system that enables seamless genome editing in R. toruloides for the first time.
The redesigned CRISPR system also simplifies marker recycling.
This work establishes a long-needed episomal plasmid platform and associated CRISPR toolkit that will accelerate metabolic engineering, synthetic biology, and fundamental studies in R. toruloides.
Genome-based bacterial taxonomy requires standardized and reproducible analytical workflows for species delineation and phylogenomic placement.
The practical deployment of standardized workflows remains a significant barrier for experimental biologists and clinical scientists.
Widely adopted tools such as Prokka, antiSMASH, and PhyloPhlAn underpin key steps in genome annotation, functional characterization, and phylogenomic reconstruction.

The practical deployment of tools like Prokka, antiSMASH, and PhyloPhlAn in routine laboratory settings, especially on Windows-based systems, remains non-trivial due to complex software dependencies and command-line centric workflows.
Existing solutions, including cloud-based platforms such as Galaxy and KBase, and commercial software suites such as CLC Genomics Workbench, partially alleviate these challenges.

Cloud-based platforms and commercial software suites may involve considerations related to data-privacy concerns, upload latency, storage quotas, shared computing resources, and recurring licensing costs.
We introduce TaxaScope, a graphical-interface-driven desktop workstation designed to support reproducible, genome-based bacterial taxonomy.

TaxaScope integrates a curated set of community-validated tools for genome quality assessment, annotation, phylogenomic inference, genome relatedness estimation, and functional profiling within a unified local graphical user interface (GUI).
TaxaScope leverages Docker- and Podman-based containerization behind a user-friendly frontend.
TaxaScope provides version-locked, standardized execution environments across computing platforms.
TaxaScope does not require manual dependency management or prior Linux expertise.
The utility of TaxaScope is demonstrated through a comprehensive re-analysis.
Expansin-like A (EXLA) proteins belong to one of the four main families within the expansin superfamily, a group of plant proteins essential for cell wall loosening.
We report, for the first time, the purification of a novel EXLA, named cpEXLA, from canihua seeds.
cpEXLA is a 29 kDa glycoprotein with a high melting temperature (Tm of 86.75 ± 1.06 °C).
The yield of cpEXLA is approximately 0.16 mg per 100 g of seeds.
Elucidation of the primary structure of cpEXLA reveals that the mature protein consists of 246 amino acids, ten of which are cysteine residues forming five disulphide bridges.
Structural studies based on 3D model prediction reveal the presence of N- and C-terminal domains in cpEXLA, which are typical of EXLAs and rich in β-sheets.
Circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy confirms the presence of β-sheets in the N- and C-terminal domains of cpEXLA.
Comparative analysis of amino acid sequences between cpEXLA and 219 similar EXLAs, retrieved from dicotyledonous genomes and transcriptomes, identified eighteen invariant amino acid residues.
Eleven invariant amino acid residues are located in the N-terminal domain, and seven are located in the C-terminal domain of cpEXLA.
Phylogenetic analysis of EXLAs in dicotyledonous species shows a close relationship between cpEXLA and other EXLAs from the Amaranthaceae family.
Phylogenetic analysis confirms that EXLA proteins are highly conserved among dicotyledonous plants.
cpEXLA represents an intriguing native tool for studying cell wall evolution and the functional role of EXLAs.
Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a common malignant tumor with a poor prognosis and limited effective therapeutic targets.

The study aimed to build a circRNA-miRNA-mRNA ceRNA regulation network of LUAD.
The study aimed to identify miRNAs and mRNAs significantly related to the prognosis of LUAD.

The Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathways of the differential LUAD-related genes were analyzed.
The circRNA-miRNA-mRNA ceRNA network of LUAD was built.

The proliferation-related ceRNA network was built.

The mRNAs were significantly enriched in 92 GO biological processes (such as cell division, cell adhesion).

The ceRNA regulation network is significant for identifying biomarkers related to the prognosis in LUAD.

Two systematic literature reviews were conducted independently in pairs.
The reviews used the BVS (LILACS and Medline), PubMed, and CAPES Journals databases.
One review focused on identifying bacteria present in the oral cavity of snakes.
The other review focused on bacteria involved in secondary infections.
The results were categorized by Old World and New World regions.
In the New World, 35 bacterial genera and 9 snake genera were reported across the included studies examining oral cavity samples.
In the Old World, 65 bacterial genera and 28 snake genera were reported in the available literature.
Regarding secondary infections in patients, 18 bacterial genera and 3 snake genera were reported in the New World literature.
In Old World studies, 21 bacterial genera and 5 snake genera were documented for secondary infections in patients.
These counts represent cumulative diversity reported across heterogeneous studies and should not be interpreted as estimates of true ecological richness.

Mammography has drawbacks as a screening tool.

Anhedonia is the blunted responsiveness to previously rewarding stimuli.
Anhedonia is a core symptom of several psychiatric disorders.
Ketamine and psilocybin have shown promising evidence in ameliorating anhedonic symptoms in clinical trials.
The Probabilistic Reward Task (PRT) was developed to objectively quantify reward responsiveness in clinical populations and laboratory animals.
The PRT was used to explore acute and sustained effects of several psychedelics and relevant pharmacological comparators on reward responsiveness in rats.
The study involved rats with n=12 per group and n=84 in total.
Reward responsiveness was significantly increased following administration of psilocybin (0.1-1 mg/kg) or ketamine (10 mg/kg) acutely.
The effect of psilocybin or ketamine on reward responsiveness persisted 24 hours after dosing.
The effects of psilocybin on reward responsiveness were blocked in a dose-dependent manner by pretreatment with the 5-HT receptor antagonist.
The effects of ketamine on reward responsiveness were not blocked by pretreatment with the 5-HT receptor antagonist.

Extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) is an emerging tumor biomarker notable for its tumor-specific amplification.
Extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA) contributes to genomic heterogeneity.
The substantial heterogeneity of eccDNAs poses a significant challenge for characterization.
Current identification tools rely predominantly on single data types.
Current identification tools often overlook the integrative potential of multi-omics layers.
Current identification tools often discard sparse but biologically meaningful signals.
We developed eccDNAOmix, an AI-empowered framework.
eccDNAOmix integrates a specialized eccDNA sequencing pipeline with multi-omics data.
eccDNAOmix evaluates the relative contributions of different biological modalities.
eccDNAOmix is based on matched tumor and adjacent normal tissues from colorectal cancer patients.
eccDNAOmix employs a masking strategy to eliminate non-biological noise.
eccDNAOmix features a multimodal deep learning model with an adaptive gated fusion mechanism.
Our model achieved robust identification performance (AUC = 0.844).
The DNA sequence modality achieved an AUC of 0.822, making it the most identifiable feature for eccDNA identification.

Biological characterization showed that eccDNAs are preferentially derived from promoter regions.
EccDNAs exhibit a significant enrichment of RNA modifications within 100 bp downstream of junction sites.
EccDNAOmix rescued hidden eccDNA fragments from conventionally discarded unmapped sequencing reads.
The rescue of hidden eccDNA fragments by eccDNAOmix was confirmed via experimental validation.
This study provides the first comprehensive characterization of eccDNAs by integrating multi-omics sequencing and eccDNA sequencing.
The multi-omics analysis demonstrates that the DNA sequence contributes the highest proportion to eccDNA identification.

The work proposes a practical computational framework for advancing discovery in colorectal cancer.
Bacterial conjugation is an important means of horizontal gene transfer in which DNA is transferred from a donor to a recipient cell by direct cell-to-cell contact.
Dissemination of antibiotic resistance in bacteria is very often driven by conjugative plasmids harboring antibiotic resistance genes.
Recent research highlighted the temporal cascade of DNA reactions that are critical for the establishment of a plasmid in the new host.
The temporal cascade includes prompt and robust induction of anti-defense genes.
The temporal cascade includes re-formation of double-stranded circular form of the plasmid after transfer as single-stranded linear DNA.
The nature of conjugation, which occurs in a mixture of cell populations, constrained the research on plasmid establishment.
Since plasmid molecules before and after transfer are indistinguishable, distinction between donor and recipient/transconjugant cells is required.
Physical separation is particularly necessary for genomic approaches.
We established a novel method exploiting a mutant donor which can be expeditiously eliminated from the conjugation mixture with simple manipulation.
Metabolomics provides direct insights into cellular physiology.
Metabolomics faces greater analytical challenges compared to genomics and transcriptomics due to the chemical diversity, instability, and environmental sensitivity of metabolites.
Conventional bulk metabolomics averages signals across cell populations, thereby masking cellular heterogeneity critical for understanding disease mechanisms.
Recent breakthroughs in single-cell metabolomics (SCM) have been driven by advances in mass spectrometry, microfluidics, isotope tracing, and spatial omics.

Future developments in SCM will require the establishment of cross-laboratory quality control frameworks.
Future developments in SCM will require the application of artificial intelligence for data interpretation.

Tryptophan plays a key role in regulating human lung homeostasis and immunity through the indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase (IDO) and aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) signalling pathways.
In patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), altered IDO and AhR activity is observed.
Altered IDO and AhR activity in COPD potentially favours infection by pathogens capable of synthesizing their own tryptophan.
This study investigated the contribution of tryptophan availability to lung infection.
A chemically defined medium with controlled tryptophan levels was developed.
The medium was used to determine bacterial metabolite consumption and excretion.
The medium was used to determine bacterial genome-wide differential gene expression.
The medium was used to determine bacterial post-transcriptional regulation.
Under tryptophan-rich conditions, we observed up-regulation of specific genes.
Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have recently been shown to possess coding potential via a cap-independent translation mechanism.
This finding challenges the traditional classification of circRNAs as noncoding RNAs.
CircRNAs are implicated directly in the pathogenesis of various diseases.
There is growing evidence of the functional roles of circRNAs-encoded peptides (circPEPs) in disease mechanisms.
Computational methods for predicting circRNAs-encoded peptides (circPEPs) remain underdeveloped.
CFCPred is a novel tool for circPEPs prediction.
CFCPred combines cluster purity-guided resampling with fuzzy voting (FV) within a traditional machine learning framework.
To address the scarcity of known circPEPs, CFCPred employs a resampling strategy that mitigates class-imbalance in the training data.
The resampling strategy generates synthetic samples based on relationships among individual samples, their nearest neighbours, and their cluster assignments.
To tackle class overlap in the testing data, fuzzy voting (FV) enables adaptive model selection and dynamic weight adjustment across the ensemble.
The adaptive ensemble integrates predictions from multiple base models to produce a robust consensus classification.
Experimental validation across multiple independent datasets demonstrates that CFCPred achieves strong predictive performance.
CFCPred provides a computational framework that can accelerate research into circPEPs and their roles in disease.
theBIGbam is a genome browser and alignment viewer designed for massive metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets.
theBIGbam takes BAM files containing read alignments together with genome assemblies in FASTA format or annotated genome sequences in GenBank format.
theBIGbam can alternatively start from raw FASTQ reads and generate alignments using a modified mapper that supports circular genomes.
The modified mapper enables seamless read mapping across genome ends.
theBIGbam can compress hundreds of gigabytes of input files 10- to 100-fold into dedicated databases while retaining key per-position information.
Key per-position information includes coverage depth and recurrent mismatches, insertions, and deletions between reads and the reference.
The compressed databases can be served to a local web browser, enabling interactive exploration of any contig in any sample.
Interactive exploration uses DNAFeaturesViewer for genome maps and Bokeh for mapping-derived features.
Contig-sample pairs available for visualization can be filtered using a range of summary metrics calculated per contig, per sample, and per contig-sample pair.
The summary metrics guide users toward the most relevant signals.
Through its interactive visualization, theBIGbam facilitates the exploration of complex datasets.
The integrated database combines assembly features, annotated features, and mapping-derived features to provide the information needed to investigate biological hypotheses systematically.
theBIGbam is designed to complement existing browsing tools like IGV and Anvi'o.
theBIGbam is particularly suited for examining misassemblies, subpopulations, microdiversity, and contig topology in large-scale datasets.
theBIGbam is an open-source Rust/Python package.
theBIGbam can be installed from Bioconda or PyPI.
The source code and documentation for theBIGbam are available on GitHub (github.com/bhagavadgitadu22/theBIGbam).
The escalating generation of global vegetable waste represents a critical loss of bioactive resources.

This review provides a comprehensive analysis of the synergistic application of microbial engineering and artificial intelligence (AI) to resolve bioprocessing bottlenecks within a food-to-food closed-loop framework.
Recent advances in engineering food-grade microbial chassis, such as Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Escherichia coli, enhance lignocellulose degradation and stress tolerance.
The integration of AI across the value chain includes deep learning-based rational enzyme design, genome-scale metabolic modeling, and intelligent process control for precision fermentation.
The hardware-software coupling of engineered strains and AI algorithms significantly enhances conversion efficiency and process robustness.
AI-driven Design-Build-Test-Learn cycles facilitate the de novo creation of enzymes with superior kinetics and strains with adaptive stress response capabilities against toxins.
Dynamic digital twin models effectively mitigate the impact of substrate variability, ensuring batch-to-batch consistency required for food applications.
This data-driven synergistic paradigm is pivotal for establishing a resilient circular bioeconomy.
The paradigm enables the reliable bioconversion of waste into high-value single-cell proteins, natural flavor additives, and sustainable packaging materials.
A major goal of the Human Genome Project is to construct detailed physical maps of the human genome.

Logic programming provides a convenient and mathematically rigorous way of reasoning about data.
Data visualization provides layout algorithms for assembling and displaying genome maps.
This paper describes numerous rules for map assembly implemented in a data-visualization system called Hy+.
